notes:
### Added

- connect.tescom.gr has a home page for visitors, in English and Greek (Greek for a Greek browser, or chosen with EN / ΕΛ): what Tescom Connect does, Actions, privacy (hosted in the EU), the Connect Cloud that is coming, questions, and plans (coming soon). Sign in is one click away.
- Activation with myTescom: sign in with your myTescom account and enter your UPS's activation code, shown in myTescom on the UPS's page. It activates that UPS on every computer you sign in on. The Activate screen lists your myTescom UPSs and which are activated. Help has an article on it.
- Actions can watch several UPSs at once: tick the ones a rule is for, or Every UPS. Each shows its serial number and where it is, so ten Primes can be told apart.
- New conditions for Actions: the battery needs replacing, the UPS is overloaded, goes to bypass, switches its output off, or reports an alarm, and an unstable supply (the mains lost a number of times within some minutes).
- Each UPS's Setup has its serial number: shown when the UPS reports it, typed from the label when it doesn't (the Prime doesn't). A UPS without one asks for it: it registers the UPS and links it to its myTescom device.
- A second UPS with the same name is numbered (Tescom Prime 2).
- Help, from the round ? button at the bottom left: how the app works, what each status means, the supported UPS series, and what to do when a UPS isn't read.
- Report a problem, from the same button: what happened in your words, a screenshot of the app and an optional file, with the app's and the UPS service's logs and what each UPS reports. Saved on this computer and sent to Tescom without signing in, and you get a report number. Also on the first screen, for when the UPS can't be found.
- The app keeps its own log file, which goes with a problem report.
- Linux: the app now includes NUT and the cloud agent, as on macOS and Windows. Add a UPS → My computer finds the UPS on USB or serial, sets it up as a service (asking for the administrator password) and can send its readings to the cloud, with nothing else to install.
- Tescom Prime: battery tests (quick, timed, deep) and stopping them, and turning the output off and on. With mains present, turning the output off moves the Prime to bypass (the output stays on); on battery it cuts power at once, so the app asks first.

### Fixed

- Dropdowns are drawn by the app, the same on macOS, Windows and Linux (on Linux they opened as a plain white list), with keyboard use as before.
- Setup's UPS commands list only commands with a name in words, as the ⋯ menu does.
- The UPS's ⋯ menu lists only commands it can name in words; NUT's internal ones (driver.killpower, driver.reload, shutdown.default) no longer show.
- Testing tools no longer show to customers: the admin tools and simulated UPSs, Start over, recording a battery test without the readiness checks, and the cloud backend's details in Diagnostics. Everything the UPS reports is folded away on the Settings page, and a crash shows a plain message with the details folded.
- Tescom Prime: a battery test started from the app no longer shows as a power cut. The Prime reports battery mode during a test; while a test the app asked for runs, it shows as a test. Any other switch to battery (a power cut, or overvoltage with mains still there) still shows as on battery.
- Tescom Prime: on a Raspberry Pi it was read only every ~7 s and often showed as waiting. The Prime ignores a request sent right after its last reply; the driver now leaves 50 ms between them.
- Tescom Prime: picking it from the list when the first search didn't recognise it now keeps its serial port, instead of setting it up with a port it can't use.
